This document guides AI agents contributing to `umami-kotlin`. It is a Kotlin Multiplatform library wrapping the Umami REST API to provide a type-safe, asynchronous, easy-to-use interface (Android, iOS, JVM, etc.). Modules: `:umami` (core), `:sample:simple-compose-app`, `:sample:terminalApp`. `:umami` packages: `api` (Umami REST API communication), `core` (HTTP client + event queue), `domain` (data models/value objects like `Hostname`, `Ip`).

Ktor for all HTTP networking; multiplatform clients (e.g., OkHttp for Android/JVM, Darwin for iOS). Kotlinx Coroutines for async/event queue. Kotlinx Serialization for JSON. `kotlin.time.Instant` for all date/time (type safety + multiplatform). Kermit for logging. Kotest for assertions: new tests must use Kotest matchers (e.g., `shouldBe`) instead of `kotlin.test` assertions. Mokkery for mocks. Builder pattern: `UmamiOptionsBuilder`. Facade pattern: main `Umami` class. Producer-consumer pattern: Kotlin `Channel` queue; background coroutine sends events to Umami API.

All contributions must adhere to [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Project built with Gradle; recommended IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA Community Edition or Android Studio. Static analysis: Detekt (`detekt/detekt.yml`, runs before git push) and Qlty (`.qlty/qlty.toml`). Ensure no new static analysis issues. Code coverage enforced with Kover; minimums in root `build.gradle.kts`. Run coverage check (command omitted here).

All new features must be accompanied by tests. Bug fixes should also include a test that reproduces the bug. Verify compile/run by running JVM tests for the modified module using `jvmTest` (no Android SDK needed):
`./gradlew :umami:jvmTest`
`./gradlew :umami-api:jvmTest`
`./gradlew :sample:terminalApp:jvmTest`
Full platform compilation/integration checks happen in CI.

Documentation: Dokka (`./gradlew dokkaHtml`). Publishing: Maven Central via `maven-publish`. Update this file if significant architectural/build changes occur.
